citation: Izady et al., Hydrogeology Journal (2015), electronic supplementary material, Fig. S4
source_variable: bedrock depth below land surface, metres (not bedrock MSL)
source_method: bedrock iso-depth lines interpreted from 320 sounding and cross-section controls reported by authors
digitization: approximate figure registration, selected checked green contour fragments, and label-guided local contour controls
georeferencing: north-up affine approximation to project Neyshabur AQUIFER.geojson feature 33; no graticule printed on Fig. S4
quality: Geometric scenario requested by user; the shallow boundary is not inferred from the paper or measured geology.
known_limitations: Contour interval is about 20 m; map labels are not measurements at every output point.
Several source raster line components merge neighboring contours, so only selected checked components are traced.
Coverage is sparse away from selected labeled contours; interpolation and absolute storage are scenario estimates.
Do not interpret cyan sounding dots as measured depth values; the source does not print numeric depths at those dots.
The supplied aquifer boundary is assumed to be shallow everywhere, including holes; an administrative or groundwater-divide boundary need not be a bedrock outcrop.
The 5m edge depth and 5km transition are explicit geometric assumptions, not field-calibrated values.
Well constraints only enforce compatibility with observed water depths; the additional 5m saturated margin and compact support shape are assumptions, not measured bedrock depths.
Synthetic boundary and grid samples are not independent observations and do not improve measured coverage.
Shallow assumed bedrock may lie above interpolated water heads; model cells then have zero saturated thickness, not confirmed observed drying.
CSV decimals encode a reproducible scenario and do not imply survey precision.
dataset_type: digitized source plus explicitly assumed shallow aquifer boundary

boundary_correction.well_lower_bound: Final D is max(tapered D, each compact local constraint). At a well, minimum D = deepest observed WATER_TABLE through Shahrivar 1404 + 5m assumed saturated margin.
boundary_correction.well_constraint_formula: B_i = 5 + (minimum_depth_i - 5) * (1 - (r/R_i)^2)^2 for r<R_i, else 5; R_i=0.95*min(distance_to_boundary_i,5000-distance_to_boundary_i). Supports cannot touch boundary or unchanged core.
boundary_correction.distance_method: nearest segment across all exterior and hole rings; local equirectangular metre projection
boundary_correction.interior_rule: At distance >= 5000m, preserve original contour-IDW depth exactly.
boundary_correction.source_interpolation: IDW squared distance over the nearest point of each original contour depth, using four nearest depth groups
boundary_correction.boundary_vertices: Every supplied ring vertex is preserved, including holes and small polygon parts.
boundary_correction.outside_controls: Retain source_depth_m for original interpolation/provenance; bedrock_depth_m is blank outside aquifer.
boundary_correction.runtime: Parse only digitized_inside/digitized_outside source_depth_m as original contours, then apply the analytic distance taper and well constraints once. Synthetic rows must not enter contour-IDW.
boundary_correction.sensitivity: Change original interior depths +/-20m then apply the same taper and fixed well constraints, preserving the 5m boundary.
boundary_correction.execution: Client-side Python in Pyodide; scripts/correct_neyshabur_bedrock.py with aquifer3d_compute.py helpers
